blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: The Why is only "Accountants copy invoices one by one into their spreadsheet at the end of each month"; a CSV export answers it, and no PDF, XLSX, XML or JSON need is stated. Drop the plugin system from What Changes, replace design.md's "Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry" with a single CSV renderer behind the route (the rejected alternative's only flaw, "not extensible", serves no stated need), remove task 1.2 ("Plugin registry discovering `src/export/plugins/`"), and remove `src/export/plugins/` from Impact. Discovering modules at start-up from a source folder also rests on an unchecked assumption: the project builds with `tsc -p .`, so the plugins would have to be found in the compiled output, not in `src/`.
findings.title: A plugin system for export formats nobody asked for

findings.evidence: - A settings page where each user picks their preferred export format.
findings.recommendation: Nothing in the Why asks users to choose a format, and with CSV as the only format the choice is empty. Drop this item, the requirement "Users choose their export format" in specs/invoice-export/spec.md, task 2.1, and `web/src/settings/` from Impact. The requirement is also not verifiable as written: scenario "A preference" says "exports use CSV" although the route is fixed at `GET /invoices.csv`, and scenario "No plugin" contradicts the design, where "CSV is the first plugin" and so is always installed.
findings.title: A per-user settings page nobody asked for

findings.recommendation: The plan adds `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM`, which serves every invoice of a month "with number, date, customer and total": a new endpoint exposing customer names, so security (who may export) and personal-data concern it, and the settings page touches user-interface. Tick the domains the plan touches so their experts review it, or keep each unticked with its reason on its line (`- [ ] <domain> — <reason>`). The spec has no scenario for an unauthenticated or unauthorized caller; whether it needs one is for the security expert once the domain is ticked.
findings.title: Every domain unticked with no reason, though the plan exposes customer data and adds a page
